title: RFID Cards Manufacturer-Direct from China — Proud Tek Pricing
summary: Proud Tek is a Shenzhen RFID manufacturing partner — specifying and quality-controlling cards, tags, labels and wristbands since 2008 and shipping to B2B buyers worldwide — so a manufacturer-direct order goes to the people who own the specification, the chip sourcing and the QC sign-off, not to a desk that resells someone else's product. Chip sourcing, antenna bonding, printing, encoding, laser engraving, quality testing and export packing run to one Proud Tek specification under one ISO 9001-certified management system, with our QC signing off every batch — the difference between a manufacturing partner that owns the spec and a reseller forwarding your purchase order. This page sets out the capability menu across product families, how buying direct compares with going through a trading company, and the certificates and QC records your procurement team can verify before the first order.
heroPoints: A manufacturing partner, not a trading desk: cards, NFC tags, UHF labels and wristbands specified, chip-sourced and quality-controlled by Proud Tek, produced on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our spec.
Manufacturer-direct pricing with no reseller layer — you pay the price a trading company would pay us, without the margin it adds for handling paperwork rather than owning the specification.

From chip to carton under one specification: chip sourcing, antenna bonding, lamination, full-colour printing, encoding, laser engraving, 100% read-verification and export packing run on contracted partner lines to Proud Tek's process spec, with the QC records to prove it.

sections.title: What ordering manufacturer-direct actually changes
sections.intro: 'Factory-direct' is the most-claimed and least-audited phrase in China RFID sourcing — plenty of storefronts using it are trading desks with a stock-photo factory. Proud Tek's version is specific: we own the specification, the chip sourcing and the QC sign-off between your brief and your loading dock, and production runs on contracted partner lines to that specification — which is why the [production visit](/about/factory/) and audit are open invitations rather than awkward requests. Buying direct changes three things — who you talk to, what you pay, and who is accountable when a reader rejects a batch. The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first, and each is [independently verifiable](/about/certifications/).
bullets: You talk to the people who specify and sign off the product — application engineering, the QC team and the production planner sit in the same Shenzhen office, so a spec question or a delivery-date commitment does not travel through a sales intermediary first.
You pay the manufacturer-direct price — the same price a trading company pays us before it adds a resale margin, so the layer that priced in someone else's overhead simply is not there.

Cost is itemised, not bundled — we break a quote into chip, antenna or inlay, card body or substrate, printing, encoding and packaging, so you can see where the money goes and trade specifications up or down with eyes open.

One specification, one system — chip sourcing, antenna bonding, lamination, printing, encoding, laser engraving, testing and export packing run under a single ISO 9001-certified management system with Proud Tek's QC sign-off at every hand-off, rather than being scattered across a broker's supplier list.

Accountability has a name — Proud Tek owns the specification and the QC sign-off; when a batch fails your reader, our engineers retune the spec and re-run it on the partner line, instead of a reseller relaying the problem to a plant it has no contract with.

bullets: RFID cards and fobs run to ISO/IEC 14443 (13.56 MHz) and ISO/IEC 11784/11785 (125 kHz LF); PVC, PET, ABS, polycarbonate, wood, metal and recycled bodies are all specified by us and produced on our partner lines, with offset or digital print and inkjet personalisation.

NFC stickers and tags use NTAG 213, NTAG 215 and NTAG 216 for URL, vCard and marketing taps, and NTAG 424 DNA when a label has to prove it is genuine with AES-128 SUN authentication (ISO/IEC 14443, NFC Forum); ICODE SLIX2 covers HF vicinity work to ISO/IEC 15693.
UHF inlays and labels use Impinj and NXP UCODE silicon to ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2v2 (860-960 MHz), encoded to the GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard for retail and logistics.

The MOQs above are typical starting points; the firm minimum depends on chip, size, finish and encoding, so we quote it in writing per program rather than post one number that is wrong for half of them.

sections.title: Buying direct vs a trading company — where the markup lives
sections.intro: A page about manufacturer-direct pricing owes you an honest account of what the middleman actually does, and the answer is 'handle the transaction,' not 'improve the tag.' A trading company forwards your purchase order to a manufacturer like us, adds a margin for the service, and passes along a product it cannot inspect, modify or expedite — it holds no specification, no chip allocation and no QC authority to do any of those things. The point below is not that trading companies are villains; it is that you may be paying for a capability your supplier does not have. When a credential carries your access-control or payment system, that gap is the whole game.

before: Your order is forwarded to a factory the desk does not own; you pay its price plus a resale margin.
Quality is whatever the unnamed plant shipped — the desk cannot inspect an inlay or retune an antenna it did not make.
Lead times and MOQs can move after you commit, because the desk is relaying someone else's schedule.
Technical questions bounce: the salesperson asks the factory, then relays an answer days later.
'Custom' means your logo on a stock tag; the chip and antenna were chosen for the desk's margin.
after: Your order reaches our production planner directly; you pay the manufacturer-direct price with no resale layer.
Every encoded unit is 100% read-verified by our QC, with a photographic QC report and the encoding log shipped alongside.
MOQ, price and lead time are quoted in writing before tooling, then held to the production traveler.
Engineering, quality and planning answer directly — the people who specified and signed off the tag, not a message relay.
Custom means an engineered antenna, substrate and finish tuned to your surface and reader, not just print.

The quality gate that makes manufacturer-direct worth it sits at step four: 100% read-verification with a QC report you can actually read.

faq.question: How do I verify Proud Tek's production model and that you are not a trading company?
faq.answer: Start by not treating an ISO certificate as proof of a production floor — the scope line decides that, and it is the line most buyers skip. Ours are published rather than sent on request: ISO 9001 98026Q00274R000, ISO 14001 98026E00200R000, ISO 45001 98026S00203R000, issuer Anhui Certification and Inspection Co., Ltd, valid to 09 June 2029, verifiable at cnca.gov.cn. Their certified scope is the sales service of smart cards and RFID tags: they establish the legal entity and its sales and supplier-management system, and production runs on contracted partner lines. What settles the production question is the arrangement itself, which we put in writing: the order-specific process split (who does what, step by step, on the production page), the partner line's own certificates supplied during quotation, and a line visit in person or by live video walkthrough — bring third-party (SGS, TÜV, Intertek) inspection if your programme requires it. Then order a sample set and put the parts on your own readers. A trading company cannot show you a specification it owns, a first article it approved or a QC sign-off it is responsible for.

faq.question: How does buying direct compare with going through a trading company?
faq.answer: You pay the manufacturer-direct price instead of that price plus a reseller's margin, and you gain a capability the middleman does not have. A trading company forwards your order to a factory it has no contract or specification with, so it cannot inspect an inlay, retune an antenna or expedite a run — it relays messages. Buying direct puts the engineering, QC and production-planning teams on the other end of your email, and makes one party accountable when a batch has to be reworked.

faq.question: What are your payment terms for a first order?
faq.answer: Standard terms are 30% T/T deposit, 70% balance before shipment. L/C at sight or 50/50 terms are available for established accounts once an order history is in place, and PayPal is accepted for sample orders under $500. Exact terms are confirmed in writing per order — send your spec and target volume and you will have them alongside the quote.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for manufacturer-direct pricing?
faq.answer: Typical minimums start at 500 pieces for RFID cards, keyfobs and wristbands and 1,000 pieces for NFC stickers and labels; UHF inlays and labels on reel stock start at 5,000, stock SKUs at 100, and formats that need custom tooling at 2,000–5,000. The firm MOQ depends on chip, size, finish and encoding, so we quote it in writing per programme; for a locked SKU the MOQ halves after the first three orders. Samples always come first, so you qualify the part before committing to a minimum.

faq.question: Can you ship directly to my country, and on what Incoterms?
faq.answer: Yes — we export directly from Shenzhen to any country on DDP, FOB or CIF terms by DHL, FedEx or UPS express, or by ocean freight for volume. Because the goods leave our partner lines, there is no extra handling hop through a trading company's warehouse; repeat buyers draw against safety stock with 3-5 business day call-offs.
